newsitem.title: CHINA: Coca-Cola says building 23rd China plant.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola says building 23rd China plant.

text.p: The Coca-Cola Co said on Wednesday it had begun construction of a $30 million bottling plant in the southwestern city of Chengdu, its 23rd in China.
The plant would bring Coca-Cola to more than 100 million people in Sichuan, China's most populous province, a company news release said.
It is part of a commitment by the Coca-Cola Co and its bottlers to invest $500 million in China through 1997, it said.
It is also the last of 10 Coca-Cola bottling facilities to be constructed by the end of 1997 under a 1993 agreement between the Chinese government and the soft drink maker.
When completed next year, the Chengdu plant would extend availability of Coca-Cola to more than 900 million people in China, representing 80 percent of the population, it said.

The plant would be 60 percent owned by Kerry Beverages, which has equity in nine other Coca-Cola bottling ventures in China, the company said. The remaining 40 percent would be held by Chengdu Hua Jin Group.
Kerry Beverages is a joint venture between Kerry Group in Hong Kong and a subsidiary of the Coca-Cola Co.
